In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the generalised quantification theory of Barwise and Cooper has been modelled in a categorical compositional distributional semantic model of natural language, in which quantified phrases and clauses are modelled as vector spaces and linear operators, and in which a compositional semantics is given for them.
we have developed a compositional model of generalised quantifier logic that is compatible with the distributional semantics of words, and we have proved the equivalence of the two models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have formalised a generalised quantifier logic in a compositional semantics with bialgebrae, and we have instantiated this formalisation in a relational setting as well as a vector space setting.
we have shown that generalised quantifier logic is a good fit for the categorical compositional distributional model of language.
we provide a categorical compositional semantics to the quantifier theory of generalised quantification and show its equivalence to the truth theoretics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
generalised quantifiers are not only a theory about natural language, but also a theory about the semantics of vector space models.
